completed_projects.description:
Develop a weak/reflexive temporal sub-language for discrete frames where G_w evaluates over the reflexive closure (y >= x) rather than the strict order (y > x). Prove completeness for this sub-language using standard Henkin canonical model methods (no chronicle construction, no IR rule), then transfer completeness to the strict system via model-theoretic argument, bypassing the succ_cofinal gap entirely.

Phase 1: Weak sub-language definition (~100 lines). G_w(phi) := phi AND G(phi), H_w := phi AND H(phi), F_w := phi OR F(phi), P_w := phi OR P(phi). Weak Until/Since with reflexive endpoints.

Phase 2: Weak axiom system (~200 lines). Derive weak axioms in the strict system. G_w(phi)->phi is trivial. Weak Z1 (FG_w(phi)->G_w(phi)) derivable from strict Z1.

Phase 3: Weak Henkin canonical model (~500-800 lines). Standard construction where each point is a distinct MCS. No chronicle, no IR rule, no gap scenario. Constant-MCS structurally impossible.

Phase 4: Z1 + IsSuccArchimedean in the weak model (~200-400 lines). Doets maximum principle (Claim 10) + compression from sum-of-zeta to single zeta (Claims 9-11).

Phase 5: Model-theoretic completeness transfer (~100 lines). IMPORTANT: Expressing strict G in terms of weak operators is impossible (U_w(phi,bot) = phi in weak semantics, so Next is not definable). Instead use model-theoretic argument: if psi is not provable in the strict system, then neg-psi is consistent in the strict system. Since every weak axiom is a strict theorem (G_w = phi AND G), neg-psi is consistent in the weak system. By weak completeness, there exists a weak countermodel. This is also a strict countermodel (same domain, same valuation, reinterpret <= as <). Contrapositive: valid under strict -> provable.

Phase 6: Integration (~100 lines). Wire weak completeness + transfer into existing pipeline.

Phase 7: Close the sorry (~50 lines). Replace the admitted limitDomSubtype_isSuccArchimedean in ChronicleToCountermodel.lean with the Henkin-derived IsSuccArchimedean, making dd_countermodel_chronicle_discrete sorry-free.

completed_projects.description:
Build first-principles FO (first-order) satisfaction infrastructure for monadic structures and close the k-equivalence sorry chain.

The current MonadicSentence type lacks variable binding infrastructure: .forall has no De Bruijn index, .lt has no variable positions, and .atom has no variable argument. This makes it impossible to define eval/satisfies, which leaves k_type_of, ktype_finite, and k_equiv_monotone as sorries. The entire Reynolds Theorem 15 pipeline (doets_lemma_1_4, finite_structures_good, one_class, chronicle_is_good) inherits these sorries through the axiomatized KEquivalenceFramework instance.

Scope:

1. Redesign MonadicSentence with proper variable binding. Options: (a) De Bruijn indices for quantifier binding, (b) two-sorted variable scheme with explicit variable positions for binary lt. The monadic case is simpler than full FO — predicates are unary, the only relation is binary <, and quantification is over a single sort.

2. Implement decidable eval/satisfies. For finite carriers and finite signatures, satisfaction is decidable. Define eval : MonadicStructure sig → Assignment → MonadicSentence sig → Bool with proper variable lookup, quantifier evaluation over Fintype carriers, and lt comparison using the structure order.

3. Close k_type_of from the semantics. Define as the set of sentences of depth ≤ k satisfied by M, converted to a canonical representative (Finset or quotient).

4. Prove ktype_finite: finitely many k-types (bounded by 2^|S_k| where S_k is the finite set of sentences of depth ≤ k over a finite signature).

5. Prove k_equiv_monotone: k-equivalence at depth k implies k-equivalence at depth m ≤ k (subset containment of satisfied sentences).

6. Close the KEquivalenceFramework instance fields (equiv_at, equiv_is_equiv, equiv_monotone, finite_types, sum_preservation) with proofs from the FO semantics, replacing the current sorry-based axioms.

7. Refactor all downstream consumers of MonadicSentence to use the new type. Verify that doets_lemma_1_4, finite_structures_good, one_class, chronicle_is_good, and the Transfer.lean pipeline still compile and that inherited sorries from k_type_of are eliminated.

Definition of done: KEquivalenceFramework instance is sorry-free, k_type_of/ktype_finite/k_equiv_monotone are sorry-free, lake build passes, and chronicle_is_good has strictly fewer sorries than before.

completed_projects.description:
Prove Doets 1989 Lemma 1.1 (finitely many formulas up to logical equivalence) and redesign KType with a finite normal form domain, closing ktype_finite and KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types.

The current KType definition uses an infinite domain ({s : MonadicFormula sig 0 // s.quantifier_depth <= k} -> Bool) which makes Fintype impossible. The correct mathematical object (Doets 1987 Chapter 1, Section 1.6-1.7) is the space of n-characteristics: for each quantifier depth k and variable count n, there are finitely many semantically distinct formulas.

Scope:

1. Define nfCount (p : Nat) (k : Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat — the number of semantically distinct monadic FO formulas of quantifier depth <= k with n free variables over a signature with p unary predicates and binary <. Following Doets 1987 Definition 1.6.1:
   - Depth 0, n vars: 2^(p*n + n*(n-1)/2) atomic types (one per truth assignment to atoms P_i(x_j) and x_i < x_j for i < j)
   - Depth k+1, n vars: 2^(nfCount p k (n+1)) (one per Boolean combination of depth-k formulas with one additional quantified variable)

2. Define NormalForm (sig : MonadicSignature) (k : Nat) (n : Nat) — a finite type of normal form representatives (Doets n-characteristics / Hintikka formulas). This can be Fin (nfCount sig.preds.card k n) or a custom inductive. Each normal form at depth 0 is a conjunction of literals over the atomic formulas P_i(x_j) and x_i < x_j. Each normal form at depth k+1 specifies, for each depth-k normal form with one extra variable, whether exists-x and forall-x versions hold.

3. Define nf_eval : NormalForm sig k n -> OrderedMonadicStructure sig -> (Fin n -> carrier) -> Prop — the semantic interpretation of each normal form. By structural recursion on the normal form.

4. Prove Doets Lemma 1.1 (the main theorem): for every MonadicFormula sig n with quantifier_depth <= k, there exists a NormalForm sig k n that is semantically equivalent (same truth value in every structure under every assignment). Proof by induction on k:
   - Base case (k=0): every quantifier-free formula is a Boolean combination of atoms; reduce to DNF over the finitely many atomic types.
   - Inductive step (k+1): a depth-(k+1) formula has the form Qx.phi where Q is forall/exists and phi has depth <= k with n+1 variables. By IH, phi is equivalent to a normal form in NormalForm sig k (n+1). The quantifier Qx applied to this normal form yields one of the depth-(k+1) normal forms.

5. Redefine KType sig k := NormalForm sig k 0 -> Bool (or equivalently Fin (nfCount sig.preds.card k 0) -> Bool). This is a function from a finite type to Bool, so Fintype (KType sig k) holds by inferInstance.

6. Redefine k_type_of to use the normal form factorization: k_type_of M maps each normal form to whether M satisfies it (via nf_eval).

7. Close ktype_finite: now Fintype (KType sig k) = inferInstance.

8. Close KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types: use Setoid.quotientKerEquivRange + Set.finite_range + Fintype.ofFinite.

9. Delete the old ktype_finite definition (dead code, mathematically impossible as stated).

10. Verify all downstream files compile (IntegerModel, OrderedSum, Transfer).

Definition of done: ktype_finite is sorry-free (or deleted and replaced by inferInstance), KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types is sorry-free, Doets Lemma 1.1 is stated and proved, lake build passes.

Literature: Doets 1987 Completeness and Definability thesis (Chapter 1, Sections 1.6-1.7: n-characteristics, Lemma 1.7.1), Doets 1989 Monadic Pi11 Theories (Lemma 1.1).
